cards.title: Feeling better isn't the finish line
cards.body: Antibiotics often make you feel better before the infection is fully treated. That's exactly when people stop, and that's the problem.

cards.title: The course length has a reason
cards.body: The doctor picks the length to treat the infection properly. Stopping early can let it come back.

cards.title: Resistance is real
cards.body: Incomplete or unnecessary antibiotic use helps bacteria become resistant. Then the next infection is harder to treat, for everyone.

cards.title: No leftovers, no sharing
cards.body: Don't save half a strip for next time or hand it to a family member. Different infections need different treatment.

cards.title: Not for every cold
cards.body: Antibiotics don't work on viruses like the common cold. Don't ask the chemist for one without a prescription.

cards.title: Side effects? Call, don't quit
cards.body: If an antibiotic upsets the stomach or causes a rash, tell the doctor. Swelling of the face or trouble breathing needs urgent help: call 112.

cards.title: Finish it as prescribed
cards.body: Unless the doctor tells you to stop, complete the course. Set reminders so doses don't slip.

takeaway: Take antibiotics only when prescribed, finish the course as directed, and ask the doctor before stopping.
share: Send this to the friend with half an antibiotic strip in their bag.
